text: DSH Web Guard（DSH Web 插件）：为 DeepSeek Harness Web 界面提供独立的密码登录入口，并将认证后的请求转发到 Harness。它支持反向代理部署和独立监听端口，可管理登录密码、会话期限、失败锁定参数及监听地址；登录状态可在设置页中查看和撤销。插件还提供原生设置页面，支持调整会话策略、踢出单个设备或让所有设备退出，并支持 TLS 配置。适合需要从浏览器远程访问 DSH Web 界面并集中管理登录会话的操作者；无需外部 API 密钥，密码可在配置中设置。

DSH Web Guard adds password login and a separate listener to the DSH Web UI. It forwards authenticated requests and supports reverse proxies. Its native settings page manages sessions, lockout options, device revocation, and sign-out. TLS is configurable.

DSH Web Guard feature “密码登录”: 插件在独立监听端口提供登录页面；登录通过后建立会话，并将请求转发至 DSH Web 上游。
DSH Web Guard feature “会话管理”: 原生设置页面展示会话，可结束单个设备的会话或让所有设备退出。
DSH Web Guard feature “调整登录策略”: 设置页可更新会话期限、失败次数阈值、锁定时长及监听地址和端口。
DSH Web Guard feature “Reverse proxy”: Forwards authenticated requests to the DSH Web upstream.
DSH Web Guard feature “Settings panel”: Registers a native settings section and icon in the DSH client.

A password gate for the DeepSeek Harness Web UI — one plugin that fixes four deployment problems at once and adds a native settings page.

@lvxianchao/dsh-web-guard README · Introduction：| Problem | Vanilla behaviour | dsh-web-guard |
|---|---|---|
| No human login | A per-process `?token=` printed to the terminal, new on every restart | One password + revocable sessions |
| `/api` returns 403 behind a proxy | The browser-trust fence requires `Host` to arrive unrewritten; NPM/Caddy rewrite it | The proxy rewrites `Host`/`Origin` to the loopback authority, which the fence accepts |
| Token lives in the journal | `journalctl \| grep token` before you can get in | Exchanged in-process; the browser never sees a token |
| UI breaks on plain HTTP | `crypto.randomUUID is not a function` outside a secure context | Injects a `getRandomValues` polyfill |

@lvxianchao/dsh-web-guard README · Introduction：Zero runtime dependencies (Node standard library only). The npm package ships prebuilt JavaScript, so `dsh plugin add` needs no toolchain; building from a checkout is a maintainer command (`npm run build`).

Requires **DeepSeek Harness `0.2.2-rc.1` or newer** (`engines.dsh: >=0.2.2-rc.1 <0.3.0`). On an incompatible host the whole bundle is skipped — for a front door that means the gate does not start, so upgrade DSH rather than removing the plugin.

@lvxianchao/dsh-web-guard README · How it works：```
browser ──HTTP(S)──> dsh-web-guard :3081 ──> DSH listener (loopback)
                          │
                          ├─ not signed in → /login
                          ├─ signed in → forward, Host/Origin rewritten to loopback

The harness fence accepts a loopback authority, so making every upstream request look like one removes the 403 entirely. Authentication happens **in the proxy**, not as a front-end overlay — a request without a session cookie never reaches the harness.

@lvxianchao/dsh-web-guard README · How it works：A small browser half (`dsh.client`) adds the management page to the harness Settings panel; the gate itself is entirely server-side and keeps working if the browser half cannot load.

@lvxianchao/dsh-web-guard README · Deployment topologies：**1. Direct, no reverse proxy** — let the plugin terminate TLS:

```yaml
config:
  listenHost: '0.0.0.0'
  listenPort: 8443
  tls:

The session cookie is issued with `Secure`. Point DNS at the host and open one port.

**2. Behind a reverse proxy (NPM / Caddy / Traefik)** — the proxy does TLS, the plugin does auth:

Set the upstream to `http://<dsh-host>:3081` and enable WebSocket support. **No Host-rewrite configuration is needed** — that is the part this plugin removes.
@lvxianchao/dsh-web-guard README · Deployment topologies：**3. Plain LAN** — HTTP plus password. Simplest, least safe: the session cookie can be sniffed on a shared network.

@lvxianchao/dsh-web-guard README · Language：The login page and the settings surfaces follow the harness language setting: the plugin reads
`preference` from the `locale` row in the profile patch file (`~/.dsh/profiles/web/cordis.patch.yml`),
which is exactly where the harness settings UI writes it. Chinese and English are
supported. With no explicit preference the pages fall back to the browser's
`Accept-Language`.
@lvxianchao/dsh-web-guard README · Theme：The native settings page is part of the harness, so it simply follows the harness light/dark choice.

@lvxianchao/dsh-web-guard README · Theme：The login and sign-out pages are standalone documents rendered before the harness page exists, so the server reads the harness choice from the profile patch (`- id: ui-theme` → `config.preference`, the row the Appearance control writes) and forces that palette before first paint. Precedence: `?theme=light|dark` → the harness preference → the operating system (`prefers-color-scheme`) when the preference is `system` or unset.

@lvxianchao/dsh-web-guard README · Configuration：| Key | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `listenHost` | `0.0.0.0` | Interface the gate listens on |
| `listenPort` | `3081` | Gate port; must differ from the harness port |
| `password` | — | Plaintext password, hashed at startup |
| `passwordHash` | — | `scrypt$N$r$p$salt$key`; takes precedence over `password` |
| `sessionDays` | `7` | Session lifetime; `0` = expires when the browser closes |
| `maxAttempts` | `5` | Consecutive failures before a temporary lock |
| `lockMinutes` | `5` | Lock duration |
| `polyfill` | `true` | Inject the `crypto.randomUUID` shim |
| `title` | `DSH Web Guard` | Heading on the login page |
| `repo` | the project repository | Link shown under the login form |
| `tls` | `null` | `{certFile, keyFile}` to serve HTTPS |

@lvxianchao/dsh-web-guard README · Configuration：Generate a hash for the config:

```bash
node -e "import('./lib/auth.js').then(m=>console.log(m.hashPassword(process.argv[1])))" 'your-password'
```

@lvxianchao/dsh-web-guard README · Security model：- Passwords are hashed with scrypt (random salt). The plaintext appears exactly once, in the generated-password log line.
- Session tokens are stored server-side as SHA-256 digests; cookies are `HttpOnly`, `SameSite=Lax`, and `Secure` when TLS is on.
- Login POSTs are checked for a same-hostname `Origin`. The session cookie's `SameSite` attribute is the primary CSRF defence.
- Repeated failures from one IP trigger a temporary lock (in-memory, cleared on restart).
- **The session table is cached on disk** (`<profile>/data/dsh-web-guard-sessions-<port>.json`, mode `0600`, atomic tmp+rename), so **restarting DSH no longer signs signed-in browsers out**. The file holds SHA-256 digests, never tokens — neither the cache nor a heap dump can mint a working cookie. The filename carries the listener port, so a shadow instance cannot overwrite the live one.
- `/logout` ends the current browser session. To revoke everything (a suspected leak, say), use the settings page's **sign out all devices** — **a restart is not a revocation any more**.

@lvxianchao/dsh-web-guard README · Security model：**This is not multi-user.** One password, one privilege level. The harness agent can execute code, so anyone who gets in has code execution on that host — which is the product's design, not a bug in the gate.

@lvxianchao/dsh-web-guard README · When the session is gone：If the session disappears (password changed, sign-out-all, or no activity within `sessionDays`), an open tab does not sit on "reconnecting" forever:

- it probes `/__guard/session` when the tab becomes visible, when the network comes back, after a WebSocket close, and every 30 seconds
- only an explicit **401** triggers a redirect — a failed fetch (offline, server restarting) never does
- the redirect carries `?next=`, so you land back where you were after signing in
@lvxianchao/dsh-web-guard README · When the session is gone：Restarts (upgrades, config changes) are invisible: the session table is restored from disk and the page reconnects on its own.

@lvxianchao/dsh-web-guard README · Settings page：The management surface is part of the harness itself: **Settings → DSH Web Guard** (the same panel that holds General, Models and Agent presets; the entry is labelled with the plugin name and carries a shield icon).

@lvxianchao/dsh-web-guard README · Settings page：- change the sign-in password (the current one is required)
- session lifetime, lockout threshold/duration — **applied on save**
- listen host/port — marked "takes effect after restart"
- live session list (source IP, browser, last activity): sign out just this device, kick another device, or sign out everywhere

@lvxianchao/dsh-web-guard README · Settings page：The page renders inside the harness React tree, so it inherits the harness light/dark theme, scrolling, focus handling and mobile layout. On a narrow screen it collapses to a single column. There is no floating button and no separate admin URL any more — the settings page is the only management surface.

@lvxianchao/dsh-web-guard README · Settings page：**Why v3 makes the settings page native.** The server half still does all the gating, but the page is now a `dsh.client` bundle: a hand-written React module (no bundler for users, React comes from the host module table) registered into the `settings.section` slot. The harness exposes no HTML-injection route into its React tree, so a first-class entry requires exactly this. The trade-off is a declared `engines.dsh` range and a browser half that a future host may skip; the server half (authentication, forwarding, the gate itself) never depends on the browser half.

@lvxianchao/dsh-web-guard README · Troubleshooting：| Symptom | Cause |
|---|---|
| `502 upstream unreachable` | The harness is down, or `listenPort` collides with it |
| Keeps bouncing to `/login` | No session cookie; make sure you use one address (an HTTP cookie is not shared with HTTPS) |
| Login succeeds then bounces back | Clock skew between the client and the host |
| `randomUUID is not a function` | `polyfill` is disabled |
| LAN can still reach the harness port | The harness is not bound to loopback — see the startup warning |
| No **Settings → DSH Web Guard** entry | The host skipped the bundle: it is older than `0.2.2-rc.1`, or the page failed to load. Check `journalctl -u dsh-web | grep dsh-web-guard` and upgrade DSH |

@lvxianchao/dsh-web-guard README · Troubleshooting：All log lines are prefixed `[dsh-web-guard]` and share the harness's journal stream. Successful requests are not logged (the Web UI polls constantly); only failures and slow requests are.
